mainTopic: The dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל about the position for קריאת שמע, the exemption for someone busy with a מצוה, and the start of the משנה on the ברכות of שמע
overview: The גמרא explains why בית שמאי read 'when you lie down and when you rise' as actual lying down and standing: otherwise the תורה would simply have said 'morning and evening.' בית שמאי use 'when you walk on the way' to exempt someone busy with a מצוה, and a חתן. This leads to a side discussion. The source is the word 'your' in 'your sitting' and 'your walking.' A חתן who marries a בתולה is exempt because he is distracted by a מצוה, unlike a man marrying an אלמנה or a man whose ship sank. A ברייתא then lists every position בית הלל allow. It tells the story of רבי ישמעאל, who sat up so the students would not think lying down is required. Three אמוראים disagree about someone who follows בית שמאי: רב יחזקאל says he fulfilled the מצוה, רב יוסף says he did nothing, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says he deserves death. A new משנה then lists the ברכות before and after שמע and says their set form may not be changed. The גמרא begins asking what the first morning ברכה says.

steps.title: Why don't בית שמאי accept בית הלל's reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that בית הלל explain both their own view and בית שמאי's פסוק. It asks why בית שמאי don't simply agree with בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense for בית הלל, since they explain their own reason and also the reason of בית שמאי. But בית שמאי, why don't they say like בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by pointing out that בית הלל have a full answer covering both פסוקים. It then asks what בית שמאי would say back. This sets up בית שמאי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל used ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ to show you read שמע in any position. They also explained בית שמאי's פסוק as 'the time when people lie down.' So בית הלל have dealt with both sides, but בית שמאי have not yet explained why they reject בית הלל's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
It makes sense / granted (introduces the side that is fine, before asking about the other side)
But (here it introduces the side that has a problem)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not attacking בית הלל. It says בית הלל's position is complete and asks only what בית שמאי would answer.

phrases.english: Gemara
Granted, Beit Hillel
explain their own reason
phrases.notes: Their reason comes from ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״: when you walk on the road you aren't lying down or standing, so any position works.

phrases.english: and the reason of Beit Shammai
but Beit Shammai

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי כְּבֵית הִלֵּל?
phrases.english: what is the reason they do not say like Beit Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית הִלֵּל קָא מְפָרְשִׁי טַעְמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why בית שמאי reject בית הלל's reading of ״בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ as only a time

steps.title: The wording 'lie down' and 'rise' means actual position
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that if the פסוק meant only a time, it would have said 'morning and evening.' Choosing 'lie down' and 'rise' means real lying down and real standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי would tell you: If so, let the פסוק say 'in the morning and in the evening.' Why does it say 'when you lie down and when you rise'? To teach that at the time of lying down, you must actually lie down, and at the time of rising, you must actually be standing.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי answer that the תורה's choice of words proves their point. A simple time would have been written as 'morning and evening.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument rests on the extra wording. The תורה had a clear way to say 'time' and did not use it. בית שמאי conclude that the words about lying and rising add a rule about the body's position.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if בית הלל were right)
When you lie down and when you rise (דברים 6:7)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way of learning פסוקים: if the תורה uses unusual wording when simple wording was available, the unusual wording is teaching something extra.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai would say to you:
If so, let the verse say
"in the morning and in the evening"
What is the meaning of "when you lie down and when you rise"?
At the time of lying down — actually lying down
and at the time of rising — actually risen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לָךְ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אִם כֵּן נֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק could have said 'morning and evening.' Saying 'lie down and rise' teaches actual position.

steps.title: What do בית שמאי do with 'when you walk on the way'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how בית שמאי explain ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״, the phrase בית הלל used as their proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי: this phrase 'and when you walk on the way,' what do they do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to בית שמאי and asks what they learn from בית הלל's proof phrase. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase in the פסוק must teach something. If בית שמאי don't use ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ to show that any position is fine, they need to explain what it is for.

keyTerms.meaning: And when you walk on the way (דברים 6:7)
What do they do with it? (how do they use this פסוק)

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai:
this phrase "and when you walk on the way"
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי הַאי וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ מַאי עֲבִיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After בית שמאי's reading is explained, asks how they handle בית הלל's proof phrase
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What בית שמאי learn from ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״

steps.title: The phrase exempts someone busy with a מצוה and a חתן
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי use the phrase for a ברייתא. 'Sitting in your house' excludes someone busy with a מצוה, and 'walking on the way' excludes a חתן. From here, someone who marries a בתולה is exempt and someone who marries an אלמנה is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need that phrase for what a ברייתא taught: 'When you sit in your house' excludes someone busy with a מצוה. 'And when you walk on the way' excludes a חתן. From here they said: someone who marries a בתולה is exempt, and someone who marries an אלמנה is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי use ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ for a different law. It teaches who is exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of learning about body position from this phrase, בית שמאי use it with ״בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ״ to exclude certain people from the obligation. The ברייתא lists someone occupied with a מצוה and a חתן. It then makes a practical distinction: marrying a בתולה exempts, but marrying an אלמנה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it (for a different teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: ״בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ means actual lying down and standing, because otherwise the תורה would have said 'morning and evening.' They use ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ for the ברייתא that exempts someone busy with a מצוה and a חתן (one marrying a בתולה, not an אלמנה).
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ is not being dropped. בית שמאי still learn from it, just a different law than בית הלל do.

phrases.english: That phrase they need
for that which was taught in a baraita:
"When you sit in your house"
excluding one who is busy with a מצוה
"and when you walk on the way"
excluding a groom.
From here they said:
one who marries a virgin is exempt
and one who marries a widow is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי use ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ for the ברייתא exempting someone busy with a מצוה and a חתן. From there, one who marries a בתולה is exempt and one who marries an אלמנה is obligated.

steps.title: How does 'walking on the way' teach the exemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא learns from 'when you walk on the way' that a חתן is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the words 'when you walk on the way' teach that a חתן, or anyone busy with a מצוה, is exempt from קריאת שמע. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from Step 4 stated the rule but did not explain it. The words of the פסוק seem to describe walking, not marriage. So the גמרא wants to see how the exemption comes out of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it implied? Where does this come out of the text?

phrases.english: How is it implied?
phrases.notes: He means: how do the words 'when you walk on the way' show that a חתן is exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source mechanism behind the ברייתא quoted in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase 'וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ' teaches that someone busy with a מצוה, such as a חתן, is exempt.

steps.title: רב פפא: like an optional trip
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the פסוק compares all cases of obligation to a trip, which is optional. So only someone doing optional activities is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is like 'the way.' Just as a trip on the way is optional, so too everything in the פסוק is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that 'the way' is an example of something optional. The פסוק obligates people in that kind of situation, not someone busy with a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Traveling is usually your own choice, not a commandment. רב פפא uses it as a model: the obligation applies when you are doing voluntary things. A חתן is busy with a מצוה, so he falls outside the model and is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Like 'the way' (a trip on the road)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Like 'the way.'
Just as a trip on the way is optional,
so too all cases are optional activities.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כִּי דֶרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק uses 'the way,' an optional activity, as its model. Only someone engaged in optional activities is obligated, so someone busy with a מצוה is exempt.

steps.title: But a trip could be for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the פסוק could also include someone traveling to do a מצוה, and the תורה still says to read שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we not also dealing with someone who is traveling to do a מצוה? And even so, the תורה said he should read שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא. A trip is not always optional, because a person might be traveling to do a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's proof depends on the idea that 'the way' always means an optional trip. But the פסוק says 'walking on the way' with no limit. It could include a trip for a מצוה, which would mean even someone doing a מצוה is obligated. That knocks down the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing with...? (introduces a challenge)
A מצוה matter, a trip for the sake of a מצוה

phrases.english: Are we not dealing
even with one who is going for a מצוה?
And even so, the Torah said: he should read.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּקָא אָזֵיל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's comparison that 'the way' is always optional.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's 'walking on the way' is unlimited and could include a trip for a מצוה. If so, the תורה obligates even someone doing a מצוה, which is the opposite of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The proof is from the word 'your'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds the proof in the wording. The תורה could have written 'when sitting and when walking.' It wrote 'your sitting' and 'your walking,' meaning your own activities. When you are doing a מצוה, you are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the תורה write 'when sitting and when walking.' Why does it say 'when you sit' and 'when you walk'? To teach that in your own sitting and your own walking you are obligated, but when it is for a מצוה you are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new proof that does not depend on the word 'way.' It points to the extra word 'your' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have said plain 'sitting' and 'walking.' Adding 'your' limits the obligation to activities that are your own business. Sitting or walking for a מצוה is not 'yours,' so a person in that situation is exempt. This answers the challenge of Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that were the meaning

steps.whatToRemember: The final source for 'someone busy with a מצוה is exempt from a מצוה' is the word 'your' in 'בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ': only your own activities obligate you.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא's 'like the way' proof is the final answer. The גמרא rejected it in Step 7, and the real proof is the extra word 'your.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the well-known rule that someone busy with one מצוה is exempt from another (עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה).

phrases.english: If so, let the Torah write
'when sitting and when walking.'
What is 'when you sit and when you walk'?
phrases.notes: The ending 'ךָ' means 'your.' That small extra ending is what the גמרא is learning from.

phrases.aramaic: — בְּשֶׁבֶת דִּידָךְ וּבְלֶכֶת דִּידָךְ הוּא דְּמִחַיְּיבַתְּ,
phrases.english: In your own sitting and your own walking you are obligated,
but for a מצוה, you are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּשֶׁבֶת וּבְלֶכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7 by moving the proof from 'way' to the word 'your.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source reading: the extra word 'your' replaces the comparison to 'the way.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'walking on the way' includes every trip, even one for a מצוה, so everyone is obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Your sitting' and 'your walking' mean your own activities. Someone acting for a מצוה is exempt.

steps.title: Then one who marries a widow should also be exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if anyone busy with a מצוה is exempt, then one who marries an אלמנה should also be exempt. But the ברייתא said he is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even one who marries a widow should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא based on the rule it just proved. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will need to explain the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that anyone busy with a מצוה is exempt. Marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה, just like marrying a בתולה. So why did the ברייתא in Step 4 obligate the man who marries an אלמנה?

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge from what was just said)

phrases.english: If so,
even one who marries a widow should also be exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ כּוֹנֵס אֶת הָאַלְמָנָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule proven in Step 8 to challenge the distinction in the ברייתא from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that one who marries an אלמנה is obligated in קריאת שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה. If being busy with a מצוה exempts a person, he should be exempt just like one who marries a בתולה.

steps.title: The groom of a virgin is distracted; the groom of a widow is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a חתן who marries a בתולה is distracted, while one who marries an אלמנה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (marrying a בתולה) is distracted, and that one (marrying an אלמנה) is not distracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9. It explains why the man who marries an אלמנה is still obligated in קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being busy with a מצוה is not enough by itself. What exempts the חתן is that the מצוה keeps his mind busy. The man marrying a בתולה is worried that he may find she is not a בתולה, so he cannot focus. The man marrying an אלמנה does not have that worry, so he is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman marrying for the first time

phrases.english: This one is distracted,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the חתן who marries a בתולה.

phrases.english: and that one is not distracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי טְרִיד, וְהַאי לָא טְרִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 about the man who marries an אלמנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone busy with a מצוה is exempt, so marrying an אלמנה should exempt too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption depends on actually being distracted. Only the groom of a בתולה is distracted.

steps.title: If distraction exempts, a person whose ship sank should be exempt too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if distraction is the reason, then a person whose ship sank should also be exempt. But רב teaches that an אבל, who is very upset, is still obligated in every מצוה except תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the reason is distraction, then even someone whose ship sank at sea should be exempt! And if you say that is true, why did רבי אבא בר זבדא say in the name of רב: An אבל is obligated in all the מצוות in the תורה except תפילין, because תפילין are called 'splendor,' as it says: 'Bind your splendor upon you'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 10. If being distracted exempts a person, then anyone who is upset, like someone who lost his ship, should be exempt as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא blocks the reply 'yes, he is exempt' by quoting רב. An אבל is surely upset and distracted, yet he is obligated in every מצוה. His only exemption is תפילין, and that comes from a special reason, the word 'splendor,' not from his distraction. So distraction alone cannot be what exempts a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Distraction, worry that keeps the mind busy
And if you will say (the גמרא heads off a possible reply)

steps.confusionAlert: The אבל is exempt from תפילין, but not because he is distracted. It is because תפילין are called 'splendor,' and splendor does not fit a mourner. That is exactly why his case proves that distraction alone does not exempt.

phrases.english: If it is because of distraction,
then even one whose ship sank at sea should also be exempt!
And if you say: yes, that is so,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: why did Rabbi Abba bar Zavda say in the name of Rav:
A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות
stated in the Torah,
except for tefillin,
since the word 'splendor' is said about them,
as it says: 'Bind your splendor upon you'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם טִרְדָּא, אֲפִילּוּ טָבְעָה סְפִינָתוֹ בַּיָּם נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 10, that distraction is what exempts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that the חתן is exempt because he is distracted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If distraction exempts, every distracted person, like one whose ship sank, would be exempt. But רב says even an אבל is obligated in all מצוות, so distraction alone does not exempt.

steps.title: Distraction from a מצוה exempts; distraction from a personal matter does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חתן is distracted because of a מצוה, while the man whose ship sank is distracted because of a personal, optional matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he is distracted by the distraction of a מצוה. Here, he is distracted by the distraction of a personal matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. It explains why the חתן is exempt but the person whose ship sank is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins steps 8 and 10 together. Only being distracted is not enough, and only doing a מצוה is not enough. A person is exempt only when a מצוה is the thing keeping his mind busy. The man whose ship sank is upset about a personal loss, so he must still read שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Distraction caused by a personal, optional matter

steps.whatToRemember: The exemption needs two things together: being busy with a מצוה, and that מצוה actually keeping the mind distracted. A חתן who marries a בתולה has both. One who marries an אלמנה or loses his ship does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule known as עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה for this case. The exemption comes from distraction caused by a מצוה, not from ordinary worry or sadness.

phrases.english: There, he is distracted by the distraction of a מצוה,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the חתן, who is busy with the מצוה of marriage.

phrases.english: here, he is distracted by the distraction of a personal matter.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the man whose ship sank.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם טְרִיד טִרְדָּא דְמִצְוָה, הָכָא טְרִיד טִרְדָּא דִרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by narrowing which kind of distraction exempts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any distraction, even over a lost ship, should exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only distraction caused by a מצוה exempts. Distraction over a personal matter does not.

steps.title: How do בית שמאי read the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and asks how בית שמאי explain the words 'when you walk on the way.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי, how do they use this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It returns to the פסוק and asks how בית שמאי read 'when you walk on the way.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption of the חתן was learned from 'when you walk on the way.' Now the גמרא wants to know what בית שמאי do with those words in their own reading of the פסוק. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking what בית שמאי do with the words 'when you walk on the way.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the discussion of the חתן, the גמרא turns back to the reading of the פסוק according to בית שמאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How בית שמאי explain the words 'when you walk on the way' in the פסוק of קריאת שמע.

steps.title: בית שמאי use the verse to exempt people on a מצוה errand
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי need the words 'when you walk on the way' to exclude שלוחי מצוה from saying שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need that verse to exclude people who are on their way to do a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. בית שמאי use 'when you walk on the way' to exempt a person traveling for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי read the פסוק as describing what a person does when he is involved in his own affairs. Someone traveling for a מצוה is not on 'your' way, so he is exempt from שמע. That is why the verse is not wasted for בית שמאי, even though they do not learn the position of the body from it.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it (this verse is needed for something else)
People sent on, or traveling for, a מצוה

phrases.english: That verse they need
phrases.notes: 'That verse' is 'ובלכתך בדרך', when you walk on the way (דברים 6:7).

phrases.english: to exclude those who are on the way to do a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִבְּעֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 13 about how בית שמאי use the verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do בית שמאי learn from 'ובלכתך בדרך'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They learn from it that someone traveling for a מצוה is exempt from שמע.

steps.title: בית הלל learn two things from the same words
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל also exempt שלוחי מצוה. They say the same verse also shows that an ordinary traveler says שמע while walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: from this itself we learn that a person says שמע even while on the way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how בית הלל read the verse. They agree about the מצוה traveler, and they also see in it a proof that one may say שמע while walking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if בית הלל also use the verse to exempt שלוחי מצוה, where do they get their rule that any position is fine? The answer is that the verse says it 'automatically.' If only a מצוה traveler is excluded, then a regular traveler must say שמע right there on the road, without stopping, standing, or lying down.

phrases.english: And בית הלל say:
From this itself, learn from it
phrases.notes: The same verse that exempts the מצוה traveler also teaches this second point.

phrases.english: that even on the way, a person also recites שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אָמְרִי מִמֵּילָא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question: if בית הלל also use the verse to exclude שלוחי מצוה, what is their source that any position is allowed?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Excluding only the מצוה traveler shows that a regular traveler says שמע on the road. So no special position is needed.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists every position allowed by בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that, according to בית הלל, one may say שמע standing, sitting, reclining, walking, or working.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: בית הלל say, people stand and recite, sit and recite, recline and recite, walk on the road and recite, and work at their jobs and recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out בית הלל's view. Any body position is fine for קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes clear what step 15 implied. For בית הלל, the words about lying down and getting up are about the time of day, not the body's position. So a person may say שמע however he happens to be, even in the middle of his work.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: בית הלל say:
People stand and recite, sit and recite,
recline and recite, walk on the road and recite,
work at their jobs and recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and spells out the בית הלל position described in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, שמע may be said in any position, even while walking or working.

steps.title: The story begins: the two rabbis switch positions
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל was reclining and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was sitting up. When it was time for שמע, each switched to the opposite position.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבי ישמעאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. They were reclining together at a meal in one place. רבי ישמעאל was leaning and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was sitting upright. When the time for קריאת שמע arrived, רבי אלעזר leaned over and רבי ישמעאל sat up.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story to show the dispute in real life. This step only sets the scene; the conversation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר leaned down to say the evening שמע, following בית שמאי, who say 'when you lie down' means lying down. רבי ישמעאל did the opposite and sat up. His switch looks strange, and the next steps explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: A story; an incident that happened

phrases.english: And there was an incident with רבי ישמעאל
and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה,
who were reclining at a meal in one place,
and רבי ישמעאל was leaning,
and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was sitting upright.
Once the time for reciting שמע arrived,

phrases.aramaic: הִטָּה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְזָקַף רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר leaned over, and רבי ישמעאל sat upright.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the בית הלל rule from step 16 being acted out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it was time for שמע, the two rabbis switched positions: one lay down, the other sat up.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה complains with a parable about a beard
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה protests that רבי ישמעאל seems to do the opposite of him on purpose, like a man who grows his beard only to annoy those who shave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to רבי ישמעאל: ישמעאל my brother, I will give you a parable. What is this like? A man to whom people say, 'Your beard is full and nice!' He answers them: 'Let it stand against those who destroy theirs.' You are the same. As long as I was upright, you were leaning. Now that I leaned, you sat up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges רבי ישמעאל's behavior. Why did he sit up just when רבי אלעזר lay down?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable, a man gets a compliment and turns it into a jab at others. רבי אלעזר says רבי ישמעאל did the same: it looks as if he changed position only to oppose him. In effect this is a challenge: 'Why are you going out of your way to do the opposite?'

keyTerms.meaning: Those who destroy (here, those who shave off their beards)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to רבי ישמעאל:
Yishmael, my brother, I will tell you a parable:
What is this matter like?
It is like a man to whom people say,
'Your beard is full!'
He said to them: 'Let it be against those who destroy theirs.'
phrases.notes: He means: I grow it only to oppose people who shave. A compliment turned into a jab.

phrases.english: You are the same:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֲנִי זָקוּף — אַתָּה מוּטֶּה,
phrases.english: as long as I was upright, you were leaning;
now that I leaned over, you sat upright.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the switch of positions described in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's choice to sit up exactly when רבי אלעזר lay down.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The switch looks as if it was done only to oppose רבי אלעזר, like the man in the beard parable.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל explains: I followed בית הלל and protected the students
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that he followed בית הלל, while רבי אלעזר followed בית שמאי. He also had to stop the students from thinking lying down is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I acted according to בית הלל, and you acted according to בית שמאי. And more than that, I worried that the students would see and set the הלכה that way for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל defends what he did. He was not opposing רבי אלעזר; he was showing the correct הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to his answer. First, the הלכה follows בית הלל, so he did nothing wrong. Second, if both of them had lain down, the students might think lying down is required, as בית שמאי say. They might then fix that as the הלכה forever, so he had to sit up to show it is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also
They will fix the הלכה for future generations

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows בית הלל: שמע may be said in any position. רבי ישמעאל sat up on purpose so students would not think lying down at night is required, as בית שמאי say.
steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל do not forbid lying down. Any position is fine. רבי ישמעאל sat up only to show clearly that lying down is not a requirement.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a teacher's actions teach the הלכה. Sometimes he must act in a way that keeps students from learning the wrong rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: He said to him: I acted according to the words of בית הלל,
and you acted according to the words of בית שמאי.
And not only that, but
perhaps the students would see
phrases.notes: They would see you lying down to say שמע.

phrases.english: and fix the הלכה that way for generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ אֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's complaint in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He followed בית הלל, the accepted הלכה, and needed to stop the students from wrongly making בית שמאי's view the הלכה.

steps.title: Why did he need a second reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל's extra words 'and furthermore' add.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and furthermore' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל added a second reason. His first reason, that he follows בית הלל, seems to be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל allow any position for שמע, including reclining. So רבי ישמעאל could have stayed reclining and still followed בית הלל. The גמרא wants to know why he had to sit up at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean
And furthermore; and not only that

phrases.english: What is 'and furthermore'?
phrases.notes: These are רבי ישמעאל's words from step 19, where he added that he had to stop the students from getting the wrong idea.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְלֹא עוֹד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second half of רבי ישמעאל's answer in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי ישמעאל needed the extra reason, if reclining is also allowed by בית הלל.

steps.title: Changing position would look like following בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: Reclining is fine for בית הלל only if you were already reclining. Switching from upright to reclined would look like following בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that בית הלל also allow reclining, so רבי ישמעאל could have stayed reclining, that is only when one was reclining from the start. But here, since you (רבי אלעזר) were upright until now and are now reclined, people would say: 'This shows they hold like בית שמאי.' The students might see this and fix the הלכה that way for generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second reason. רבי אלעזר had switched from upright to reclining just for שמע. If רבי ישמעאל had stayed reclining next to him, the students would think they both hold like בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל have no problem with reclining as such. The problem is the change of position. Moving from upright to reclined just for שמע sends the message that reclining is required, which is the opinion of בית שמאי. To avoid the students learning the wrong הלכה, he had to make a visible point.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (bringing up a possible objection)
Learn from this, conclude from this
The law for all future generations

steps.whatToRemember: What a רב does in front of students can teach a wrong הלכה, even when the act itself is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בֵּית הִלֵּל נָמֵי אִית לְהוּ מַטִּין,
phrases.english: And if you say: Beit Hillel also hold reclining is fine,
that applies when he was reclining from the start.
But here,
since until now you were upright
phrases.notes: 'You' is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. He sat upright and then leaned over; רבי ישמעאל had been leaning from the start.

phrases.english: and now reclined,
they will say: conclude from this
they hold like Beit Shammai,
lest the students see
and fix the law for generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בֵּית הִלֵּל נָמֵי אִית לְהוּ מַטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lying down after being upright would look like following בית שמאי, and students might set the הלכה that way. So he had to sit up.

steps.title: רב יחזקאל: either way, you have fulfilled the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב יחזקאל teaches that one who follows בית שמאי or one who follows בית הלל has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יחזקאל taught: If he acted like בית שמאי, he has done it. If he acted like בית הלל, he has done it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: what if someone said שמע the way בית שמאי require? רב יחזקאל says that still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows בית הלל, but according to רב יחזקאל, doing it the בית שמאי way is not a failure. Either way, the person was יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: He has done it (he fulfilled the מצוה)

phrases.english: Rav Yechezkel taught:
if he acted like Beit Shammai, he has done it;
like Beit Hillel, he has done it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to a general rule about following בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who said שמע according to בית שמאי has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: רב יוסף: following בית שמאי counts for nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees and says that one who acts like בית שמאי has done nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If he acted like בית שמאי, he has not done anything at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף argues with רב יחזקאל. In his view, doing it the בית שמאי way does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of step 22. For רב יוסף, the opinion of בית שמאי is not a valid option at all. Someone who followed it would have to say שמע again the right way.

keyTerms.meaning: He has done nothing at all

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף does not mean that sitting or standing is forbidden. He means that following בית שמאי's opinion as the rule does not count.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
if he acted like Beit Shammai,
he has done nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יחזקאל in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who follows בית שמאי has not fulfilled the מצוה.

steps.title: רב יוסף's source: the משנה about the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף begins a proof from a משנה about someone whose head and most of his body are in the סוכה while his table is in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone whose head and most of his body were in the סוכה, and whose table was inside the house: בית שמאי say it is invalid, and בית הלל say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a משנה about סוכה to support his view. Here the גמרא quotes the case and the argument; the part that proves his point comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about whether eating like this counts. רב יוסף will use what follows in this משנה to show that, for בית שמאי, doing it the other side's way counts for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ בַּסּוּכָּה
phrases.english: As we learned: one whose head and most of him were in the sukka
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in סוכה.

phrases.english: and his table inside the house,
Beit Shammai invalidate,
and Beit Hillel validate.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the source for רב יוסף's statement in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that following the other side's opinion counts for nothing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about a person whose head and most of his body are in the סוכה while his table is in the house.

steps.title: The visit to רבי יוחנן בן החורנית
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the quoted משנה, בית הלל tell a story: the elders of both schools visited רבי יוחנן בן החורנית. He was sitting with only his head and most of his body in the סוכה, and nobody objected.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: There was a story. The elders of בית שמאי and the elders of בית הלל went to visit רבי יוחנן בן החורנית. They found him with his head and most of his body in the סוכה and his table inside the house, and they said nothing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה that רב יוסף began using in the previous step. Here בית הלל bring a story to show that sitting this way in the סוכה is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל argue that even the elders of בית שמאי were present and stayed silent. Their silence seems to show that they also accepted this way of sitting. This sets up בית שמאי's reply in the next step, and that reply is the real point of רב יוסף's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
There was an incident where the elders of Beit Shammai went
and the elders of Beit Hillel

phrases.aramaic: לְבַקֵּר אֶת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן הַחוֹרָנִית,
phrases.english: to visit Rabbi Yoḥanan ben HaḤoranit,
they found him with his head and most of his body in the sukka
and his table inside the house,
and they said nothing to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the סוכה משנה that רב יוסף began in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that one who acts like בית שמאי has done nothing
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about רבי יוחנן בן החורנית

steps.title: בית שמאי say he never fulfilled the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי deny that the story proves anything. They say the elders actually told him that if he sat this way, he never fulfilled the מצוה of סוכה. רב יוסף learns from this that following the rejected opinion counts for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Is there a proof from there? They actually said to him: If this is how you have been acting, you have never in your life fulfilled the מצוה of סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's story. For רב יוסף, this line is the heart of his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי held that anyone who did not follow their opinion did not fulfill the מצוה at all. In the same way, now that the הלכה follows בית הלל, someone who follows בית שמאי has done nothing. This supports רב יוסף against רב יחזקאל.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there a proof from there? (a way of rejecting a proof)
They also; here it means they actually did say something
The commandment of dwelling in a סוכה
In all your days, ever in your life

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, the משנה shows that following the opinion that was not accepted means the מצוה was not done at all.

phrases.english: They said to them: And is there proof from there?!
phrases.notes: Now בית שמאי are answering בית הלל.

phrases.english: They too said to him:
If you have been accustomed to act in this manner,
you have never in your life fulfilled the מצוה of sukka.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם וּמִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית שמאי reject בית הלל's story from step 25. That rejection is the evidence רב יוסף needs.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that one who follows the rejected school has done nothing
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית שמאי's statement in the משנה in סוכה that he never fulfilled the מצוה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Within the משנה, בית שמאי reject בית הלל's story as a proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elders were not silent. They told him he had not fulfilled the מצוה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: following בית שמאי deserves death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק goes further than רב יוסף. He says that one who acts like בית שמאי deserves death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: One who acted like בית שמאי deserves death.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives the strongest opinion so far about someone who follows בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יחזקאל said such a person fulfilled the מצוה. רב יוסף said he did nothing. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is even worse than doing nothing, because he went against the accepted ruling of בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Acted according to the words (opinion) of

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a court punishment. As the next step shows, it means he deserved the danger that came upon him.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: עָשָׂה כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי — חַיָּיב מִיתָה.
phrases.english: One who acted in accordance with Beit Shammai is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third and stricter opinion after רב יחזקאל and רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who acts like בית שמאי against בית הלל deserves death.

steps.title: Proof from רבי טרפון on the road
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings proof from our משנה. רבי טרפון lay down to say שמע like בית שמאי and was put in danger by robbers. The חכמים told him he deserved it for going against בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in the משנה: רבי טרפון said, I was traveling on the road, and I lay down to read שמע like בית שמאי, and I put myself in danger because of robbers. They said to him: You deserved to lose your life, because you went against the words of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב נחמן בר יצחק's harsh statement from the earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים did not just say רבי טרפון failed to fulfill the מצוה. They said he deserved to be in mortal danger. That fits רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that following בית שמאי is worthy of death.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views about someone who follows בית שמאי. רב יחזקאל says he fulfilled the מצוה. רב יוסף says he did nothing. רב נחמן בר יצחק says he deserves death.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Tarfon said:
I was coming on the road
and I reclined to recite in accordance with the words of Beit Shammai
and I endangered myself because of the highwaymen,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּדַאי הָיִיתָ לָחוּב בְּעַצְמְךָ,
phrases.english: they said to him: You deserved to be liable with your life,
for you transgressed the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that following בית שמאי deserves death
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about רבי טרפון and the חכמים' response

steps.title: New משנה: the ברכות around קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. In the morning there are two ברכות before שמע and one after. In the evening there are two before and two after. It then mentions a long one and a short one.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In the morning one says two ברכות before שמע and one after it. In the evening one says two ברכות before it and two after it. One long and one short.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion is done, and a new משנה starts. It tells us how many ברכות are said with קריאת שמע at each time of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was the time and position for saying שמע. Now the משנה moves to the ברכות that surround it. The morning has three ברכות in total and the evening has four. The words 'one long and one short' are short and unclear, and the גמרא will explain them.

phrases.english: MISHNA: In the morning one recites two blessings before it
and one after it.
And in the evening one recites two blessings before it
and two after it.
One long and one short.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בַּשַּׁחַר מְבָרֵךְ שְׁתַּיִם לְפָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the debate about following בית שמאי ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the morning there are two ברכות before שמע and one after. In the evening there are two before and two after.

steps.title: Do not change the form of a blessing set by the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that you may not change the shape the חכמים gave a ברכה. You cannot shorten a long one or lengthen a short one. You cannot drop a required closing ברוך or add one where none belongs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where the חכמים said to make a ברכה long, you may not make it short. Where they said to make it short, you may not make it long. Where they said to close it with a ברוך, you may not leave out the closing. Where they said not to close it, you may not add a closing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from Step 29 keeps going. It gives a general rule: you must keep each ברכה exactly in the form the חכמים set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 mentioned 'a long one and a short one.' Here the משנה explains why that matters: the length is fixed, and so is whether the ברכה ends with a closing line. Both are part of the fixed form of the ברכה, not personal choices.

keyTerms.meaning: to close (end the ברכה with a closing 'ברוך אתה ה׳…')

steps.whatToRemember: The form of a ברכה, both its length and whether it has a closing ברוך, is set by the חכמים. You may not change it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of תפילה: the fixed wording and structure of ברכות must be kept, and a person cannot reshape them on his own.

phrases.english: A place where they said to make it long —
one is not permitted to shorten;
where they said to shorten — one is not permitted to lengthen.
where they said to close — one is not permitted not to close;
phrases.notes: 'Close' means ending the ברכה with a final line that begins 'ברוך אתה ה׳'.

phrases.english: where they said not to close — one is not permitted to close.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְהַאֲרִיךְ — אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַצֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in Step 29 by giving the general rule behind 'a long one and a short one.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The length of a ברכה, and whether it has a closing ברוך, may not be changed from what the חכמים set.

steps.title: What words of blessing does one say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks what the actual ברכה is that one says before שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What ברכה does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a simple question: what are the words of the ברכה before שמע? This question sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said how many ברכות there are, but not what they say. The גמרא wants to know what the ברכה is about and how it is worded. This is a question asking for information, not an attack on the משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What blessing does he say?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְבָרֵךְ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and asks about the wording of the ברכות listed in Step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The wording and content of the ברכה said before שמע in the morning.

steps.title: רבי יעקב in the name of רבי אושעיא begins to answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces the answer from רבי יעקב, who quotes רבי אושעיא. His actual words come in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי אושעיא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer by naming who is giving it: רבי יעקב, quoting his teacher רבי אושעיא. The answer itself comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only names who is speaking, but it starts the answer to Step 31. The content, which is based on a פסוק, follows next. Keep the question 'what ברכה?' in mind while you read on.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the question in Step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is credited to רבי יעקב in the name of רבי אושעיא. Its content follows in the next text.
